claims.text: Monte Carlo-induced chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr will form HfTi clusters.
Monte Carlo-induced chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr will form TiZr clusters.
The induced HfTi and TiZr clusters will produce ordered B2-like structures.
The induced short-range-order clusters will form percolative high-conductivity pathways.
Formation of the short-range-order clusters will reduce local lattice distortion.
Reduced local lattice distortion will limit phonon scattering.
Short-range ordering will modify the high-frequency phonon density of states.
The reduced scattering, percolative pathways, and modified phonon density of states will increase lattice heat conductivity.
The short-range-ordered alloy will have approximately 12% higher lattice heat conductivity than the random defect-free alloy.
Short-range ordering will produce a quantifiable reduction in atomic-displacement scattering.
Available analytical predictions for HfNbTaTiZr typically model a random, perfect, defect-free bcc crystal without short-range-order clustering.
The random-alloy analytical baseline has high lattice distortion.
The simulation-based approach will capture short-range-order effects more realistically than idealized analytical models.
The hypothesis is applicable to bcc HfNbTaTiZr from approximately 0 to 200 K.
The hypothesis is applicable to bcc HfNbTaTiZr from 300 to 1200 K.
The hypothesis is applicable at high temperature to a HfNbTaTiZr specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
The mechanism should not be extended directly to fcc high-entropy alloys without additional validation.
